title: Privileged Roles Endorsement and Key Management Verification Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: Capture the end-to-end product requirements, acceptance criteria, and a compact sign-off playbook for privileged access controls, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC mappings for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, and customer-keying verification (KMS/HSM). Background: Several enterprise prospects have requested explicit evidence and reproducible steps that show Redwood Private meets their audit and key custody controls. Scope: - SSO/SAML integration flows (IdP metadata exchange, user attribute mapping for groups/roles, assertion lifetime, logout behaviors) - RBAC model and role-binding tooling for Private control plane and host agents - Audit logging scope (what events are recorded, retention, exportability, tamper-evidence) - Customer-managed keys (CMEK) workflows, HSM attestations, key rotation, and emergency key-migration plan - Sign-off evidence artifacts and checklist items needed for customer onboarding and compliance packages Out of scope: cryptographic algorithm changes, major KMS vendor integration beyond AWS KMS/HashiCorp Vault (we will document gaps), full SOC2 report creation.
requirements_clarifications: IdP requirements: Must support SAML 2.0, metadata URL ingestion, and allow group claims via 'groups' attribute or SCIM v2 for group sync.
RBAC: Role model must allow separation of machine vs human principals; role bindings scoped to org/project/environment; deep links to console for role grants.
Audit logs: Immutable append-only log exported to customer S3/GCS with signer metadata; minimum event set defined in acceptance criteria.
CMEK/HSM: Support import and use of customer keys (encrypt/decrypt operations) with HSM-backed key origin and support for key rotation without service interruption.
Operator access: Support short-lived elevated access tokens for support engineers with recorded justification and automatic expiry.
Failure modes: Define rollback path to Redwood-managed key if customer key becomes unavailable, with alerts and customer approval gating.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Successful end-to-end SAML login with at least two IdP vendors (Okta, Azure AD) using test tenant and documented metadata exchange steps.
RBAC: Ability to create, list, and revoke role bindings via Console and API; test case where a developer is denied 'deploy' action but allowed 'read' after role adjustment.
Audit logs: Demonstrable export to customer S3/GCS bucket; logs include actor, action, resource, timestamp, request_id, and signature/hash for tamper-evidence.
KMS/HSM: Customer-provisioned key used to encrypt secrets at rest; perform a live key-rotation in staging with zero downtime and validate decryption of existing objects.
Operational: Security review completed and signed by Security and Legal; playbook contains PRs, runbook links, test artifacts, and sample signed attestations.
Documentation: Step-by-step onboarding guide and checklist added to internal Confluence and a customer-facing checklist in Drive.
Telemetry: Console shows token-level cost and a per-route log of key-usage events; alerts fire on failed key operations.
Pen test: No critical findings from targeted access-control tests run by internal red team prior to sign-off.

risks_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: Supporting SCIM group sync increases implementation time but reduces IdP-specific mapping support; prioritized SCIM for enterprise rollouts.
Risk: Immediate support for every HSM vendor expands QA scope; mitigate by certifying patterns for AWS CloudHSM and Vault HSM PKCS#11 first.
Trade-off: Retaining audit logs for longer retention increases storage cost; we will offer tiered retention as add-on to balance customer needs.
Risk: Failure to rotate customer key could impact availability; introduce automated pre-checks and a simulated rotation in staging as gating criteria.
